faults.team: A drug in the wrong cubicle

doomed.heart_attack: The artery was opened in time. The heart had already lost too much muscle.
doomed.brain_bleed: The bleed was too big. Neurosurgery said so before anyone scrubbed.
doomed.stroke: The clot was too big for the drug. The brain swelled in the night.
doomed.variceal_bleed: The bleeding never stopped. Not with blood, not with the scope.
doomed.meningitis: The antibiotics went in on time. The infection had a day's head start.
doomed.organophosphate: Too much poison, swallowed hours before anyone found out.

haemolysed.result: Potassium 7.2, dangerously high. Lab note: sample slightly haemolysed.
haemolysed.call: Lab here. Potassium of 7.2 on {patient}. Sample's a bit haemolysed, but we have to ring it through.
haemolysed.treat: Calcium, insulin and dextrose went in for a potassium that was never high. A burst sample. The repeat would have said 4.1. The sugar dropped instead.
haemolysed.repeat: The repeat potassium is 4.1. The first sample burst on the way. You didn't treat a number. Good.

wrong_patient.result: Haemoglobin 5.8, very low. Blood group B positive.
wrong_patient.call: Lab here. Haemoglobin of 5.8 on {patient}. Shall we cross-match?
wrong_patient.treat: Two units went in for a haemoglobin that belonged to someone else. The label was wrong. So was the blood group.
wrong_patient.repeat: The repeat haemoglobin is normal. The first tube was another patient's, labelled with the wrong sticker. Nobody got the wrong blood. Good catch.

typo.call: Lab here. Sodium of 13 on {patient}. It's flagged, so I'm ringing.
typo.treat: Strong salt water went in to fix a sodium of 13. Nobody alive has a sodium of 13. It was 131, typed with a finger missing.
typo.repeat: The lab checked: it was 131, typed wrong. Nobody alive has a sodium of 13. You noticed. Good.

real_critical.call: Lab here. Critical result on {patient}. You'll want to see it now.
real_critical.treat: You treated it straight away. It was real, and it fit the patient.
real_critical.repeat: The repeat says the same thing, twenty minutes later. It fit the patient the first time. Those twenty minutes were theirs.

readback.ask: Priya reads it back: "For cubicle {wrong}, Doctor?" {patient} is in cubicle {right}.
readback.correct: "Cubicle {right}. Say it back." She does. The right drug goes to the right patient. Boring. Perfect.
readback.nod: You nodded. The drug went to cubicle {wrong}. {other} got something meant for someone else, and {patient} waited for theirs.

forgotten.handover: Night team's handover: "Casualty's quiet." The board disagrees.

open: Doctor? Tell me. Just tell me straight.
We only went down for tea. Ten minutes. What happened?
Your face is saying it. Don't let your face say it. You say it.
They called us back up. Nobody calls you back up for good news, na?
plain: Okay. Okay. Was there pain at the end?
Thank you for not making me guess. Can I see them?
I have to call everyone. How do I even say this on the phone?
This morning we were arguing about the TV remote. This morning.
jargon: I don't understand any of that. Is that bad? Is someone alive or not?
Speak normally, please. I'm not a doctor. I'm just family.
You're saying words. I'm asking you one thing.
nurse: The nurse told me. She held my hand. Where were you?
She sat with me. You were busy, I suppose. Everyone's busy.

choices.plain: Sit with them and say it plainly
choices.nurse: Ask Sister Priya to tell them

after.plain: You stay until the rest of the family comes. It's the worst ten minutes of the shift, and the right ones.
after.jargon: They nod at words they don't understand. Priya takes over, and gives you a look you'll remember.
after.nurse: Priya does it well. It should have been you.

fault.you: Later, you read your own notes twice. They say the same thing both times.
fault.wait: They waited too long for a doctor. Today, that doctor was you.
fault.lab: The result didn't fit the patient. You treated it anyway.
fault.team: The drug went to the wrong cubicle, and you nodded it through.
fault.nobody: Nobody could have stopped this. You'll still think about it tonight.

family.morgue: The porters take {patient} to the morgue. By the time you look up, the name is on the wall by the desk.

you: M&M on Friday. {patient}, from today's casualty, is on the list. Bring the notes, not excuses. Nobody's hanging you. We're learning.
Saw today's casualty list. {patient}. M&M, Friday, eight sharp. I'll be there. So will the chai. You'll be fine. Not today, but you will.
lab: M&M on Friday: {patient}. The lab sent a wrong result and we treated it. Both halves of that sentence are on the agenda.
team: M&M on Friday: {patient}. A drug went to the wrong cubicle. Read-backs exist for a reason. Bring Priya, she'll want to be there.
